hit: - **Most-accommodating floor selection (direction-aware)** `[Option A, owner directive 2026-07-21]`. Where jurisdictions' code floors differ on a parameter, the regulatory-stratum determination anchors on the **most accommodating available value, read per the parameter's accessibility direction** — best-for-the-user, not largest-number: the widest minimum corridor, but the *lowest* maximum threshold height and the *gentlest* maximum ramp slope. The parameter's direction is to be recorded with the determination, and the passed-over floors remain visible as the jurisdiction spread (they are code-baseline facts, not discarded evidence). **Where the accessibility direction is population-contested** — e.g. flush thresholds aid wheeled mobility but remove the tactile cues cane users rely on; heavy acoustic absorption aids hearing-aid users but degrades echolocation; brighter light aids low vision but harms photosensitive users — **most-accommodating selection is inapplicable: no single value is anchored; the conflict is recorded via the conflicts machinery, and the jurisdiction spread is rendered with each population's direction stated** (suppressing the divergence would itself be an error, `mission-and-epistemics.md`). `[LANDED 2026-09-13 — migrations 078/079 and `assess_cell.compose_value()`. Where the engine cannot compose a value it records WHY in `specifications.value_note`, so a contested direction is distinguishable from an unrecorded one — the four decline-reasons were all a bare NULL before 079. hit: **The Design Modes weight the hierarchy asymmetrically by scale.** Universal Mode is a code-floor raised by population-level evidence wherever evidence supports a value above the floor. **The Population scale is where source-ranking does its substantive work** — the evidence hierarchy adjudicates the best-practice value and range there. The Person scale is occupational-therapy resolution of the individual's own functional needs — assessment and clinical-reasoning evidence, not parameter-value-ranking; the population range informs the assessment but does not bound the answer, which may fall outside it (commitment 4). The evidence and design axes therefore remain orthogonal, but under *scale-conditioned weighting*: the axes stay independent, while which evidence carries the most weight is conditioned by the design scale in play. Operational detail is in `governance/evidence-methodology.md` §§1.4, 1.6, 1.7.

The critical design decision is: Auracast infrastructure (conduit + power) must be specified at DD stage even though IEC 60118-17 is not published. The cost of retrofit conduit after construction is 10–40× the cost of DD-stage provision. This is a DAR principle application — cross-reference Part 10 §10.1. hit: **Opus 4.6 synthesis note (2026-03-29):** Synthesis reviewed across all three merged sections. Four findings. (1) THIN-BASE confirmation: zero Tier 1 evidence for any DBL built-environment specification in any language. GAP-DBL-BE-01 (P1 OPEN) correctly flags this. All DBL specifications must carry THIN-BASE disclosure. This is not remediable by further literature search — the evidence does not exist. The population is too small and heterogeneous for RCT-level research to be feasible. Lived experience evidence (Co-1) is co-primary here per project-standards. (2) The Protactile spatial requirement (≤600mm face-to-face, armless chairs, ≥1500mm per communication pair) is a genuinely novel provision not found in any building standard worldwide. It derives from a single community source (Clark/Nuccio). Despite the thin evidence base, the specification is biomechanically grounded (tactile communication requires physical contact; physical contact requires proximity; proximity requires clear floor space). Recommend: specify as Co-1 with THIN-BASE and frame as “emerging best practice” rather than “established provision.” (3) The JA close-range signing (接近手話, 500–1000mm) spatial requirement is distinct from ASL/BSL spatial requirements and from Protactile. This confirms that DBL spatial design cannot be calibrated from a single signed language’s proxemics — consistent with the deaf-spatial-design Opus synthesis finding. (4) CONFLICT: vibrotactile floor systems (for DBL alerting) vs TWSI tactile paving (for VIS/DBL wayfinding) is correctly identified. This is the most evidence-rich BPC in the compendium (20+ key sources, 24 jurisdictions, Tier 1 IDeA Center anthropometric research). Five findings. (1) The 1524 mm ADA rejection is correct and well-evidenced (IDeA Center, Summer Foundation/UTS, Flemmer 2025 NZ). The bathroom BPC Opus synthesis provides the resolution: Kennedy et al. 2015 (Tier 1) demonstrates vertical bars produce smallest COP deviation; bilateral provision serves both transfer directions. The guidebook should specify both horizontal AND vertical as the combined best practice, not choose one. (3) The IT three-tier framework (accessibility/visitability/adaptability) and DK three-quality-level framework (A/B/C) are structurally analogous to the guidebook’s own Universal Mode/1/2 hierarchy. This convergence should be explicitly noted in Part 1 §1.4 as international precedent. (4) The Clemson et al. 2023 Cochrane review (38% fall reduction from OT-delivered home hazard reduction) is the strongest single piece of evidence supporting the guidebook’s core premise that OT involvement in built environment design produces measurably better outcomes. This should be prominently cited in Part 1 §1.3 and Part 9 §9.2. (5) No cross-population conflict identified for MOB provisions. MOB turning circles, ramp gradients, and door widths are beneficial or neutral for all other populations. MOB is the only population code with zero conflict flags across all synthesised BPCs. Evidence confidence: HIGH (Tier 1 anthropometric data, Tier 3 Cochrane systematic reviews, 24-jurisdiction convergence on core provisions).

The conflict arises only with sensory-seeking provisions in dementia settings, where stimulating environments may increase agitation. Route to cross-population-conflict-mapper. (3) PAS 6463:2022 is correctly identified as the sole national standard operationalising this framework. No other jurisdiction has equivalent regulation. This means all NDV sensory specifications in the guidebook exceed any mandatory requirement — they are Tier 4–5 (beyond-code best practice). text: RULE: Disability populations are not uniform. Every person within a population code has a unique experience and unique functional limitations, even where there
hit: RULE: Disability populations are not uniform. Every person within a population code has a unique experience and unique functional limitations, even where there is significant overlap with others who share the same condition. There are different ways to struggle with mobility, different ways to be blind, different ways to have MS, different ways to be autistic, different ways to have dementia, different ways to experience PTSD. There is no generic ideal for any population. Specifications provide ranges and starting points — not definitive answers. It is rare for a disability to be experienced in isolation; co-occurring conditions are the norm. Every item specification must acknowledge functional variability within the population and discuss how co-occurrence affects the design parameter, because that is the lived reality of the people the guidebook serves. Population codes are a high-level organizing principle: at Universal Mode they are comprehensive (mapping all considerations); at Population Mode they offer insight (what to think about for a known population); at Person Mode they step aside because a person is not defined by their disabilities — OT works bottom-up from functional impairments because everything must be uniquely tailored to the individual.

Tier 1 = primary research with intervention-level or biomechanical control (OT-prioritized, not OT-exclusive, per D-E); Co-1 = lived experience / participatory design (CRPD Art. 4.3, co-primary with Tier 1); Tier 2 = synthesis — (a) systematic reviews / meta-analyses AND (b) named-organisation evidence-based standards; Co-2 = OT professional body CPGs (co-primary with Tier 2); Tier 3 = lower-control primary clinical research + grey-literature primary research (supporting; rarely the sole basis — T3-alone never reaches `stated`, per the tier3-stated-threshold DR); Tiers 4–6 = the regulatory stratum (international standards, national frameworks, statutory codes) — walled off from best-practice anchoring; convergence-not-evidence. The evidence hierarchy determines what constitutes best practice. Where higher-tier evidence exists, it governs.

hit: RULE: Best practice means the most accommodating, thoughtful, respectful, dignified, and usable condition achievable for the disabled person. Best practice is determined by the evidence hierarchy — Tier 1 primary research, Co-1 lived experience, Tier 2 synthesis (SR/MA + named-organisation evidence-based standards), Co-2 OT CPGs — not by code consensus. Codes are Tier 6: the compliance floor, not the aspiration. Code consensus across jurisdictions establishes what most codes agree on; it does not establish what is most accommodating or most dignified. A BPC best_practice_synthesis that derives its value solely from code consensus is a weak-band (○) best-practice claim — "best practice as currently known," valid only when flagged code-derived with the convergence-not-evidence caveat, and never rendered unflagged or above the weak band (amended 2026-07-21, owner directive, Option A; `decisions/DR-2026-07-21-evidence-architecture-option-a-execution.md`). An unflagged or full-strength code-consensus best-practice claim is in error. The test: does this specification provide the most accommodating, dignified, usable condition the evidence supports — or does it merely reflect what codes agree on?

hit: RULE: Adversarial review is a truth-instrument bound to evidence, never a plan-instrument. An adversarial pass may be commissioned ONLY against a diff that (a) wrote rows to the research tables (`search_executions`, `search_candidates`, `evidence_sources`, `source_slug_links`, `evidence_population_match`, `source_value_extractions`, `specifications`, `convergence_assessment`, `jurisdictional_values`, `case_studies`, `economics_entries`) or (b) authored or amended a synthesis artifact (`references/bpc-reasoning/*`, `best_practice_synthesis`, a rendered determination page). Plans, critiques, censuses, handoffs, registers, session records, Decision Records and this ledger are not adversarial-pass subjects; they receive the mechanical gates already registered and nothing more. The rule was earned by measurement: **at least ten fresh-context adversarial passes ran between 2026-07-14 and 2026-08-19, and not one examined research output**, because there is none — every research table stands at zero rows. The fresh-session independence convention (`workplan/2026-08-15-adversarial-brief-pr103.md` §0, "Run this in fresh context. Do not read the authoring session's reasoning first") is epistemically correct AND is the mechanism guaranteeing a new session per critique, so critique → plan → critique became the tightest loop in the repository. The one counter-example is the standard to copy: `sessions/session_2026-07-26-energy-conservation-rest-points-seating-adversarial.md`, the only pass ever run on research output, produced **seven sustained findings in a single session**, all against the author's own admitted batch, catching error in both directions — a T1-candidate under-tiered at T3 and a no-participants discussion piece over-tiered, plus one dataset admitted twice under two ref_ids and a circular value. Its own diagnosis is the thing this rule protects: *"a claim pitched at a confidence the retrieval didn't earn."* **The agonist needs no construction: R1-R15 already compel the authoring session to file its complete affirmative case as rows.** The antagonist attacks that recorded case through named lenses — existence, fidelity, independence, tier, population, contrary-finding, recognition by the population served, and query-shape — and the cheapest agonist-antagonist mechanic is blind-then-compare: re-grade tier and population-match independently BEFORE seeing the author's grades, then diff. A pass whose subject is a plan cannot be wrong about anything a reader could check.

Every person within a population code has a unique experience and unique functional limitations, even where there is significant overlap with others who share the same condition. There are different ways to struggle with mobility, different ways to be blind, different ways to have MS, different ways to be autistic, different ways to have dementia, different ways to experience PTSD. There is no generic ideal for any population. Specifications provide ranges and starting points — not definitive answers. It is rare for a disability to be experienced in isolation; co-occurring conditions are the norm. Every item specification must acknowledge functional variability within the population and discuss how co-occurrence affects the design parameter, because that is the lived reality of the people the guidebook serves. Population codes are a high-level organizing principle: at Tier 0 they are comprehensive (mapping all considerations); at Tier 1 they offer insight (what to think about for a known population); at Tier 2 they step aside because a person is not defined by their disabilities — OT works bottom-up from functional impairments because everything must be uniquely tailored to the individual.', '2026-04-24 23:38', 'solo_author_pre_launch', 'legacy/none/none', 100, 'ACTIVE', 'NA', '[]', '[]', '["references/project-standards.md \u00a7Core Doctrine (locked)"]', '["(seeded record; original alternatives not captured at rule authoring; reviewable)"]', 'Seeded from project-standards.md §Core Doctrine (locked) at A12 Session 2 (2026-04-30 13:20).
